questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the role of the judiciary in relation to the Indian Constitution?
choices: It ensures that the Constitution remains unchanged for all time
It interprets the Constitution and protects its core values
It amends the Constitution without any restrictions
It creates new constitutions whenever needed
questions.solution: The judiciary interprets the Constitution and ensures its core values are upheld, which is essential for maintaining its integrity and relevance. The first option is incorrect because the Constitution can be amended through proper procedures. The third and fourth options are wrong because the judiciary does not have the authority to amend or create constitutions independently.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a feature of a flexible constitution?
choices: It can be amended by a simple majority in Parliament

questions.solution: A flexible constitution allows for easy amendment, typically by a simple majority in Parliament. Other options describe procedures for more significant or rigid amendments.

questions.stem: Which of the following best explains the significance of the 'basic structure' theory in the Indian Constitution?
choices: It allows the legislature to amend any part of the Constitution
It prevents the judiciary from interpreting the Constitution
It defines the fundamental principles of the Constitution that cannot be amended
It allows the judiciary to change the Constitution without any restrictions
questions.solution: The correct answer is that the 'basic structure' theory defines the fundamental principles of the Constitution that cannot be amended. This is because the theory ensures that certain core elements of the Constitution remain untouched even during amendments. The other options are incorrect as they either suggest unlimited power to amend or restrict the judiciary's role in a way that contradicts the theory.

questions.stem: The Constitution has provisions that are both flexible and rigid. Which of the following best explains why some parts of the Constitution are made rigid?
choices: To allow quick changes for new circumstances
To protect fundamental rights and key features from easy alteration
To make it easier for the government to pass laws
To ensure that all amendments require a referendum
questions.solution: Rigid provisions are meant to protect fundamental rights and key features of the Constitution from being easily changed. Flexible provisions allow for easier amendments to address new situations. The Constitution does not require a referendum for amendments, and making it easier for the government to pass laws is not the purpose of rigidity.

questions.stem: What does the theory of the basic structure of the Constitution imply about the power of Parliament to amend the Constitution?
choices: Parliament can amend any part of the Constitution without any restrictions
Parliament cannot amend the Constitution at all
Parliament can amend any part of the Constitution, except those that form the basic structure
Parliament can only amend the Preamble and the Seventh Schedule
questions.solution: The theory of the basic structure implies that Parliament can amend any part of the Constitution except those that form the basic structure. The basic structure cannot be amended under any circumstances. The other options misinterpret the theory of basic structure.

questions.stem: The Indian Constitution allows for amendments but makes the process complex. What is the underlying principle behind this design?
choices: To ensure the President has ultimate authority
To make sure only the ruling party can amend the Constitution
To ensure that only elected representatives decide on amendments
To allow a constitution commission to propose changes
questions.solution: The design ensures that only elected representatives, not external bodies or the President, have the authority to amend the Constitution. This upholds the principle of parliamentary sovereignty. The other options contradict the Constitution's provisions.
